title: Should Apartments Join Food-Waste Collection?
text:
Source A - Expand Collection to Apartments
A city pilot collected food scraps from 1,100 apartment households for six months. Participating buildings sent 19 percent less trash to the landfill, and contamination in the food-waste bins fell from 14 percent to 6 percent after clearer signs were installed. The sanitation department recommends expanding gradually and providing building managers with training.

Source B - Delay Expansion
A property association argues that apartment collection should wait. It says some buildings have little space for extra bins and that managers may face complaints about odor. The association recommends another year of study but provides no contamination records, cost estimates, or data showing that odor complaints occurred during the pilot. It does suggest testing smaller bins in buildings with limited storage.
